text: Cano is a lifelong National City resident and member of SUHI Class of 1980, a Red Devil forever!

Cano served as founder of the Community and Police Relations Commission and Chair of the Civil Service Commission. Cano worked for the Department of Defense for 35 years, completed numerous deployments to the Middle East.
Cano understands, being a former Councilmember (Vice-Mayor), election is a commitment of quality service to our community and should not be about personal ego or political aspirations.
Cano has continued to be out in the community, sensing and seeing your needs, not just at election time.
Cano believes that the City’s business is your business and needs to be conducted in a professional, objective, and truly transparent fashion.
Cano believes our City needs to become more “Business Friendly” to be able to provide the level of services our residents, businesses and visitors deserve.
National City needs dependable services, not more politics as usual.

text: I, Ditas Yamane, am running for re-election as Councilmember - District 3 of the City of National City. As a longtime resident, I understand our issues and concerns about public safety, housing, homelessness, and business assistance programs in our district.

I care deeply about our community and have worked to make a positive impact by working to secure grant funds to improving El Toyon Park, building the Filipino Plaza, creating a conservation garden, adding street lights, and implementing safer walkways for us to enjoy.
It’s my goal to see our families enjoying our parks and playgrounds, taking advantage of the programs and resources our city has to offer, and feeling proud to call this community home.
I serve in leadership positions as Governing Board Chair of Sweetwater Authority; as Vice-Chair of San Diego Community Power. I am also the CEO of my own real estate agency.

It’s my priority to listen to your concerns, understand them, and work to find solutions with meaningful action. Together, let’s build a community that is safe, welcoming, and united, a place where families thrive, neighbors support one another, and everyone has the opportunity to succeed.
I am honored to serve you.

Ditas Yamane

text: My name is Ed Nieto, and I respectfully ask for your vote for National City Council, District #3.

I am a lifelong National City resident who attended local schools, including Sweetwater High School, before graduating from San Diego State University. My father was a shipyard welder, and my mother was an elementary school cafeteria worker. They taught me hard work, honesty, and respect for every dollar. Those blue-collar values continue to guide my commitment to our community. I'm National City at heart.

For 39 years, I served as a government accountant, gaining proven experience analyzing revenues, evaluating expenditures, strengthening financial accountability, and solving government fiscal and operational challenges. My career focused on protecting taxpayer dollars to help maintain the financial stability needed for essential government services.

Today, National City faces a projected $13 million budget deficit. I will bring the government financial and operational experience our City Council needs to identify problems early, make responsible financial decisions, restore fiscal stability, and implement meaningful performance measures.

I will serve with integrity, transparency, accountability, and a commitment to results. Together, we can build a stronger, safer, and more financially secure National City that ensures Public Safety, Affordability, and Quality of Life.
